row.task_instruction: Process a molecular dynamics trajectory file to create a supercell structure with systematically sorted atomic positions. Use the trajectory file "benchmark/datasets/I-ReaxFF/test/md.traj" as input and replicate the unit cell structure in three dimensions (default 1x1x1 replication). The program should identify individual molecules within the structure using distance-based connectivity analysis, then reorder all atoms by grouping them first by molecule type, then by element type following the priority order C, O, N, H. Save the resulting sorted supercell structure to "pred_results/pred_sort_atoms_mol.vasp" in VASP format and generate a summary report in "pred_results/pred_sort_atoms_mol.txt" containing information about the number of molecules, molecule types, total atom count, and replication parameters.

row.task_instruction: Perform molecular optimization using Bayesian Illumination to discover diverse small molecules with high QED (Quantitative Estimate of Drug-likeness) scores. Load the initial molecular population from the SMILES database file "benchmark/datasets/Bayesian-Illumination/data/smiles/ZINC_first_1000.smi" and evolve the population through iterative generations using genetic operations, surrogate model predictions, and acquisition function guidance. Filter molecules based on structural validity criteria (5-50 heavy atoms, allowed elements C, N, O, S, P, F, Cl, Br, I), calculate physicochemical descriptors (molecular weight, LogP, TPSA), and assign molecules to niches in a 3-dimensional descriptor space using a 10x10x10 grid. Use a Random Forest surrogate model with Expected Improvement acquisition function to efficiently explore the chemical space while maintaining diversity across niches. Run the optimization for a maximum of 10 generations or 1000 fitness evaluations, whichever is reached first, and save the final archive of optimized molecules to "pred_results/pred_illuminate.csv" with columns for SMILES, fitness values, niche indices, and generation numbers.

row.task_instruction: Perform polymer synthesis simulations using monomer reactants from the OpenMacromolecularGenome dataset to generate polymer repeat units through various ring-opening polymerization and metathesis reactions. Load the monomer SMILES data from the CSV file in the benchmark/datasets/OpenMacromolecularGenome directory, classify each monomer based on its substructure patterns (lactam, cyclic ether, cyclic olefin, cyclic carbonate, cyclic sulfide, terminal diene, and conjugated di-bromide), and simulate polymerization reactions for each applicable monomer type including ring-opening of lactam (reaction 11), cyclic ether (reaction 12), cyclic olefin (reaction 13), cyclic carbonate (reaction 14), cyclic sulfide (reaction 15), acyclic diene metathesis/ADMET (reaction 16), and Grignard metathesis method/GRIM (reaction 17). Save the final consolidated results to 'pred_results/pred_get_reactant_bag_other_reactions.csv' with columns for reaction_idx, reactant_1, reactant_2, and product, where the product column contains the canonical SMILES representation of the generated polymer repeat unit.

row.task_instruction: Perform a comprehensive evaluation of OA ReactDiff molecular diffusion model results for transition state generation and chemical reaction prediction. Analyze optimized transition states from "benchmark/datasets/OAReactDiff/demo/example-3/opt_ts/" by computing pairwise RMSD similarity matrices and performing K-means clustering analysis (6 clusters) to identify structural patterns. Load and analyze reference clustering from "cluster.json", generated transition state quality metrics from "generated_ts_quality.csv" (RMSD and energy differences), barrier energies from "barrier.csv", and Hessian summary data from "summary.csv" (imaginary frequency analysis). Analyze generated reaction xyz files from the "generated/" directory, extracting molecular formulas and collecting sample reaction information. Compare generated transition states against ground truth structures using RMSD metrics. Catalog IRC structures from the "irc/" directory. Save all evaluation results including RMSD matrices, clustering analysis, quality statistics, barrier analysis, Hessian summary, generated structure analysis, and ground truth comparisons to "pred_results/pred_demo.json" in JSON format.
